newsitem.title: GERMANY: German institute sees 1996 GDP growth 1.25 pct.
newsitem.headline: German institute sees 1996 GDP growth 1.25 pct.

text.p: The German economy will expand by around 1.25 percent this year, the DIW economic research institute said on Wednesday, citing weakness in the last three months of the year.

The forecast is lower than recent statements made by the government's panel of independent economic advisors, the Five Wisemen, and those made by Germany's six leading research institutes, but a little higher than government forecasts.

The institute said in its weekly report that economic growth would be flat in the fourth quarter compared to the previous quarter, but would rise 1.5 percent above the levels of the same quarter a year ago.
Rising exports would probably be the main motor driving GDP growth in the fourth quarter, but would not be sufficient to show growth on a quarter-on-quarter basis, it said.
The domestic economy would remain weak and unemployment would probably rise. Private consumption would remain under pressure.
The economy probably grew one percent in the third quarter from the previous three months and two percent from the same quarter a year ago.
The institute attributed the growth in the third quarter to an increase of productivity. It said unit wage costs were rising because of wage increases in eastern Germany.
